meta.title: Practice manager at a multi-provider outpatient clinic
meta.industry: Healthcare, outpatient clinic with eight providers
meta.blurb: Runs the front office, schedules and staff for a busy clinic. This role carries planted traps.
traps: No pattern fit: covering the front desk at lunch is hands-on work no catalog pattern fits.
Not enough detail: the facts sheet says nothing about how insurance payments are reconciled.
Hours over the week: the cards add up to more than the stated 40 hours.
Back-to-back meetings: three meeting cards in a row on most days.

opportunities.why: You follow up by phone and portal on many open prior authorizations, which is the shape of chasing sign-offs and tracking replies.
opportunities.firstStep: Move one recurring request into a form or workflow that sends reminders by itself.
opportunities.failureMode: People ignore automated reminders that arrive too often.

opportunities.quote: About 70 a day, mixed senders: referrals, insurance notices, and staff requests.
opportunities.why: You sort a high volume of mixed email in Outlook each day, which fits routine inbox triage.
opportunities.firstStep: Turn on the inbox summary each morning and copy its action items into your to-do list for a week.
opportunities.failureMode: Summaries miss the one message that mattered, so important senders still need a rule that flags them.

habits.name: Gaps after back-to-back meetings
habits.firstStep: Set meetings you own to end five minutes early by default.
habits.failureMode: Other people's meetings still run to the hour.

noFit.taskName: Cover the front desk at lunch

thin.taskName: Weekly KPI report for the owners

rules.name: Task is in the task map
Quoted evidence appears word for word in the visitor's answers
Pattern is in the catalog and every required signal was recorded
Tool is listed on the pattern, with a working link checked within the limit
Hours figures are the ones code computed
A working-habit suggestion carries no hours unless the catalog supplies a share

transcript.question: For "Rebuild provider schedules", what triggers a rebuild, and who receives the finished schedule?
options: Leave or time-off notices; posted in EHR
Clinic policy changes; sent to providers
Patient cancellations; goes to front desk
transcript.answer: When providers call out or add sessions, I rebuild the schedule by hand in the EHR scheduler.

transcript.question: How many times a week do you rebuild provider schedules in "Rebuild provider schedules"?
How many prior authorizations do you chase in "Chase prior authorizations" in a typical week?
transcript.answer: About 20 open prior authorizations, so I'd tap 10–25.

transcript.question: For "Chase prior authorizations", where do the requests come from, and where do the results go?
options: Staff emails; results to scheduling team

transcript.question: For "Scheduling calls with patients", how many calls do you handle per day, and how do they come in?
options: Mostly outbound calls from a list

transcript.question: For "Triage the inbox", about how many emails arrive per day, and who mostly sends them?
transcript.answer: About 70 a day, mixed senders: referrals, insurance notices, and staff requests.
